text:
maya: Heads-up — scale-down started evicting GPU nodepool in eu-west-1 during the spike at 09:12. A bunch of inference pods got rescheduled to cpu nodes and are failing startup. CA logs show aggressive unneeded-node detection :eyes:

devops-bot: [alert] 2212345680 - autoscaler: terminated nodes: 3 (gpu-eu-west-1-*) due to scale-down, reason: unneeded, metric: low-usage

sam: seeing the same. Pods stuck Pending earlier, then a bunch got force-evicted. kube-events show NodeAffinity + taints on gpu pools causing restart storms. Not all pods tolerate the taint.

jia: quick dump from the autoscaler controller logs I grabbed: 
```
I0324 09:11:58 autoscaler.go:215] ScaleDown: candidate gpu-eu-west-1-azb/node-pool-3 - unneeded for 9m12s
I0324 09:11:58 autoscaler.go:220] Node has local storage: false, pods not daemonset: 8
I0324 09:11:58 scale_down.go:89] draining node: 3 pods to evict, some have nodeSelector: nvidia/gpu=true
```

jia: current flags on prod CA (for reference): 
```
--expander=binpacking
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=2m
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true
--max-empty-bulk-delete=5
```

maya: right now the combination of short unneeded-time + binpacking means gpu nodes that are lightly used but still needed for affinity get culled. We killed throughput for a few customers.

sam: proposals: bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 30m, set --expander=least-waste for gpu pools, and maybe disable skip-nodes-with-local-storage so CA considers more options before deleting? Also consider setting a separate autoscaler profile for gpu pools.

jia: +1 on separate profile. We can annotate nodepool with autoscaler-mode=ml-gpu and run a second CA with tuned flags (less aggressive). For quick mitigation I can patch prod CA to: 
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m
--expander=least-waste
--max-empty-bulk-delete=1
```
and monitor for 30m. Would reduce churn but slow reclaim.

leo: also check cluster-autoscaler --node-group-auto-discovery filters. We accidentally included a transient test-gpu pool last week which had short-lived jobs. That made binpacking think GPUs were disposable. Removing that pool from discovery helped in staging.

maya: action items: jia will roll the quick CA flag patch to prod canary (1/3 replicas) and watch eviction rate, leo will remove test-gpu from discovery in staging and open PR to exclude it from prod, sam please compile a list of impacted customers and podspec issues (taints/affinity). I'll open an incident so SRE + CS can coordinate.

jia: will patch in 5m, will post rollout progress.

sam: compiling list now, will DM maya with urgency.

maya: thanks, folks. If the quick patch doesn't help we should schedule a short maintenance window to pin critical inference services to dedicated gpu-nodepools until we fix autoscaler profiles. :thumbsup:

(devops-bot reaction) :thumbsup: on jia's patch
